source_row.rationale: CDC states that adult peripheral IV catheters do not need routine replacement more frequently than every 72–96 hours and lists clinically indicated-only replacement in adults as an unresolved issue. Regardless of schedule policy, the site requires regular assessment and prompt replacement for infiltration, phlebitis, infection, malfunction, or other clinical indication.
source_row.source_detail: Adult peripheral catheter replacement: no need more often than 72–96 h; clinically indicated-only replacement remains an unresolved CDC issue; site should be replaced for clinical indications; accessed 2026-08-14.
